subject: general
question: According to the Census 2011 , which of the following is the third-lowest state in terms of literacy rate?
solution:
**The correct answer is 'Rajasthan'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan:**

 
 
• According to the Census 2011, Rajasthan has the third-lowest literacy rate among the states in India.
 
• The literacy rate in Rajasthan was recorded at 66.11%.
 
• This rate reflects the number of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• Various factors contribute to the low literacy rate in Rajasthan, including socio-economic challenges, gender disparities, and limited access to educational resources in rural areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar:**

 
 
• Bihar had the lowest literacy rate according to Census 2011, with a literacy rate of 63.82%.
 
• Bihar has been historically challenged by poor infrastructure, high poverty rates, and limited educational facilities, contributing to its low literacy rate.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh had a literacy rate of 70.63% as per Census 2011, which is higher than that of Rajasthan, making it not the third-lowest in literacy.
 
• The state has implemented various educational programs and initiatives to improve literacy rates, especially in rural and tribal areas.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim:**
 
 
• Sikkim had a significantly higher literacy rate of 82.20% according to Census 2011, thus it does not fall into the category of states with low literacy rates.
 
• Sikkim's relatively small population and focused educational policies have contributed to its higher literacy rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Literacy rate is a crucial indicator of a region's socio-economic development and human capital.
 
• Improving literacy rates involves addressing various challenges including poverty, gender inequality, and accessibility to quality education.
 
• Government initiatives such as the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and the Right to Education (RTE) Act have been implemented to improve literacy rates across India.
 
• Rajasthan has been focusing on schemes like the Rajasthan State Literacy Mission Authority to enhance literacy among adults and children in the state.
